title: Common Wards & Small Mendings
summary: Sound, practical wards for any household. Recommended to new tenants. — R. A.

pages.text: Draw the thread through the wax three times, {~each time against the light~}, and the seam will hold {~through any weather~} until the cloth itself gives out.
Chalk drawn along the sill keeps out draughts, {?vell-mites?}, and {~the smaller sorts of ill will~}. Renew at {~each new moon~}.
A latch so charmed will not lift for any hand {~it has not been introduced to~}. To {~introduce a hand~}, speak {?Varre?} {~and the bearer's name~} at the keyhole.
For cracked crockery. Warm the pieces by the hearth, {~press the edges close~}, and breathe along the line {~until the crack forgets itself~}.
Knot the thread above the bed. Bad dreams {~catch in the knots~} and are {~gone by morning~}; burn the thread {~at the year's end~}.
{~Every ward has a seam.~} Find it with {?brannowort?} smoke, {~then speak the latch's own word back to it~}. No door so kept {~will refuse you~}, and none {~will remember you passed~}.
pages.authorNote: Outlier. Readable on purpose: a player who lands here should start to wonder what the Board wanted with this book.
